study.title: Cognitive and affective interaction with somatosensory afference in acupuncture–a specific brain response to compound stimulus
study.study_design: Crossover within-subject fMRI experiment with two conditions (REAL and PHNT); participants randomly and evenly assigned to REAL-PHNT or PHNT-REAL order
study.randomization: Participants were randomly and evenly assigned to the crossover design of REAL-PHNT or PHNT-REAL
study.blinding: Participants in PHNT condition were given contextual manipulation to induce needling credibility; blinding of participants to sham condition was assessed via structural interviews; no mention of experimenter blinding
study.population: Twenty-five healthy, right-handed adults (16 men, 13 women; 27.8 ± 3.4 years old) without previous experience of acupuncture
study.inclusion_criteria: Right-handed adults; no previous experience of acupuncture; age 19 or above
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) age below 19 years; (2) mental or respiratory syndrome, claustrophobia, depression, bipolar disorder, anorexia nervosa, or a generalized psychiatric history within the past year; (3) poor eyesight with uncorrected vision; and (4) respiratory syndrome due to pulmonary vascular disease and physical causes

arms.dropouts: 2 excluded due to excessive head movement (over 2 mm displacement between successive image volumes); 2 excluded due to distortion of raw BOLD data with scanner issues; 6 excluded from clinical analysis due to lack of needling credibility in PHNT (only 19 of 25 reported needling credibility)
Same exclusions as REAL arm (crossover); 6 of 25 excluded for not reporting needling credibility

conditions.timepoint_exact: during 420 s fMRI scan with repeated needling stimulations
conditions.scan_context: task-fMRI during manual acupuncture needle stimulation at left ST36 with concurrent video display of the procedure

conditions.timepoint_exact: during 420 s fMRI scan with contextual manipulation only
conditions.scan_context: task-fMRI during contextual manipulation only (no needle insertion); video of needling displayed; acupuncturist mimicked needle insertion and rotation
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Explicitly stated that the needle was not inserted into the acupoint. The acupuncturist only mimicked needle insertion and rotation movements while a video played, with no physical contact or skin penetration occurring. This is a pure contextual/visual manipulation with no tissue engagement whatsoever.

conditions.timepoint_exact: inter-stimulation interval; randomized timing of acupuncturist hand approach prior to actual stimulation
conditions.scan_context: anticipatory period before needle stimulation; inter-stimulation interval between hand approach and stimulation: 5.9 ± 1.7 s for 24 stimulations; 6.0 ± 1.6 s for 22 stimulations

interventions.penetration_exact: inserted into the acupoint (ST36) before the MRI scan started
interventions.manipulation_exact: manually performed 24 or 22 needle stimulations by rotating the needle at approximately 1 Hz for 2 s; inter-stimulation interval between stimulations: 17.0 ± 2.2 s for the 24 stimulations; 19.0 ± 2.9 s for the 22 stimulations
interventions.needle_retention_exact: needle inserted before scan started and removed after completion of scan; scan duration 420 s
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Participants watched the video stream for the needle stimulation at their left leg, which was visual information for the therapeutic context (i.e., contextual manipulation)

interventions.stimulation_type: contextual manipulation only; no needle insertion
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: left ST36 (Zusanli) — acupuncturist mimicked procedures at this location but needle was not inserted
interventions.penetration_exact: needle was not inserted into the acupoint (ST36)
interventions.manipulation_exact: The acupuncturist mimicked the acupuncture procedures of needle insertion and rotation in synchronizing with the acupuncturist's action in the video clip during the PHNT session
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: not intended; needling credibility was induced via contextual manipulation
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: PHNT was performed identically to REAL from the participant's point of view, except that the needle was not inserted into the acupoint (ST36). To ensure participants' needling credibility without needling insertion, we played the recorded video clip from the participant's REAL session or the best-matched participant's REAL session
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: only contextual manipulation; PHNT led to visual afferent and needling credibility without somatosensory afferents by displaying a video for needling stimulation with verbal instruction inducing a context of acupuncture treatment

sham_details.sham_device_exact: recorded video clip from participant's REAL session or best-matched participant's REAL session displayed during scan; acupuncturist mimicked needle insertion and rotation
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: acupuncturist mimicked acupuncture procedures of needle insertion and rotation in synchronizing with the acupuncturist's action in the video clip
sham_details.sham_deqi_intended_exact: no deqi intended; needling credibility was induced via visual/contextual manipulation
sham_details.sham_credibility_procedure_exact: Needling credibility for PHNT was assessed by structural interviews at the end of the experiment; only 19 participants who reported needling credibility were included in the analysis

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports 'n_total_enrolled = 25' and 'n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging = 15'. The exclusion pathway is: 25 enrolled, 4 excluded due to head motion (n=2) or scanner issues (n=2), leaving 21; then an additional 6 excluded for lack of PHNT needling credibility, leaving 15 pairs. However, the credibility criterion yielded 19 of 25 who reported needling credibility. It is unclear whether the 19 credibility-qualifying participants overlap with the 21 retained after imaging QC, or whether the final n=15 represents the intersection of both exclusion criteria. The paper states 'Fifteen pairs of REAL and PHNT scans were used for further analyses' after imaging exclusions, and 19 participants after credibility exclusion; the final n=15 for neuroimaging analysis likely reflects the intersection.

In the results section (Section 3.6), the paper states for PHNT: 'CA1 showed marginal positive correlation with the expectation scores (r = 0.50, p = 0.06)' using Pearson's r notation; and earlier states 'CA1 in PHNT was positively correlated with the expectation scores (ρ = 0.57, p = 0.03)' using Spearman's ρ notation. These two values for the same construct in PHNT are inconsistent and may reflect different analyses or a reporting error. Both values are preserved in the extraction.

Figure 6 caption reports CA1 vs SA2 partial correlation as ρ = 0.73 (p = 0.04), whereas Table 3 reports the same as ρ = 0.73, p < 0.01. There is a discrepancy between the figure caption and the table for the p-value of the CA1–SA2 partial correlation in REAL. Both values are preserved.

Table 2 reports CA1–SA1 partial correlation (controlling for SA2 and CA2) as ρ = 0.69, p < 0.01. Table 3 reports the same pair (controlling for SA2, CA2, and expectation) as ρ = 0.84, p < 0.01. These are separate analyses with different sets of controlled variables and are extracted separately.

The paper reports 'r = 0.75, r < 0.01' for the CA1/CA2 concordance vs. PHNT HR decrease correlation (Figure 5C). The second 'r' is almost certainly a typo for 'p', i.e., p < 0.01. This is flagged and the extracted value preserves the paper's original wording.
Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the manuscript. It is unclear whether adverse events were monitored or whether the absence of reporting implies none occurred.

The paper does not report exact group-level mean ± SD or median values for heart rate changes in beats per minute (bpm) for REAL or PHNT, only significance levels and correlations. Figure 4B shows approximate values graphically but exact numeric values are not given in the text or tables.
The paper does not report the absolute expectation questionnaire scores by arm. Only correlation coefficients between expectation scores and IC parameter estimates are reported.

Voxel-wise GLM results for PHNT (Figure 3A) are shown in a figure but no coordinate table for PHNT voxel-wise results is provided in the manuscript. Only IC-wise GLM coordinate tables are provided. PHNT voxel-wise activation spatial maps appear only as a figure.

The paper states '25 healthy, right-handed adults (16 men, 13 women)' in the Methods section, which sums to 29, not 25. This appears to be a reporting error in the paper itself. The number 25 is used consistently throughout the manuscript for total enrolled participants.

Supplementary Figure 1 is referenced multiple times to describe the REAL and PHNT experimental setups, including visual information about needle position and contextual manipulation procedure. This supplementary figure was not provided in the extracted PDF pages and full procedural details of the setup may not be fully captured.

The paper uses both Pearson's (r) and Spearman's (ρ) correlation notation across results, sometimes without explicitly specifying which test was used for a given result. The extraction preserves the notation used in the paper.

The IC-wise GLM group-level test for IC9 (CA1) is described as a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (V = 120, p < 0.01 for REAL; V = 116, p = 0.01 for PHNT), whereas IC22, IC23, and IC29 use one-sample t-tests. The reason for this difference (presumably non-normal distribution for IC9) is not explicitly stated in the methods.

Figure 3A shows voxel-wise GLM group average maps for REAL and PHNT separately as brain images. No coordinate table accompanies the voxel-wise GLM results. The neuroimaging coordinate table (Table 1) only reports IC-wise GLM results.

Table 1 Z-scores are described as 'unnormalized z-statistics of peak voxels from the temporal concatenated ICA', not z-statistics from the GLM parameter estimate test. These are ICA component z-scores reflecting the strength of each region's contribution to the IC spatial map, not the group-level GLM test statistics.
